title: Regional failover forensics — geo-split & policy TTL
content:
Goal: capture breadcrumbs from the 2026-03-09 regional failover that caused increased 5xxs for hosted-api customers in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. This is a personal scratchpad — rough, actionable, and intended for follow-up during postmortem.

Summary (short):
- Timeline started ~2026-03-09T17:22Z. Spike in 5xxs traced to smart-routing fallback taking a long path (cross-region) instead of local backup pool. Latency soared and some requests hit incompatible quantized model variants leading to OOMs and 502s.
- Immediate mitigation: forced routing policy TTL reset + pinned eu-west-1 traffic to local dedicated pool (route-eject on policy id rp-889) at 2026-03-09T18:05Z — error rate back to baseline by 18:27Z.

Raw observations / breadcrumbs:
- Alerts: PagerDuty triggered for "hosted-api error-rate-high" at 2026-03-09T17:25Z. Root alert tags: model=redwood-open-13b, route=default-chat.
- Console spike: Console dashboards showed per-token latency 4x baseline, token cost increase flagged by Optimize.
- K8s events around the time: node autoscaler churn in eu-west-1, a rolling restart in dedicated-gpu-pool-eu-west-1 triggered by a maintenance job (kube-drain by ops) at 17:18Z.

Commands I ran (timestamps local to my shell at the time):
- Quick health checks:
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/health" | jq .
  # returned ok but per-route health: 
  curl -sS "https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/routes/default-chat/status" | jq .

- Inspecting route policy resolution for a sample request-id:
  rtrctl resolve --request-id=20260309-17:26:03-abc123 --format=json
  # snippet output: (paraphrased)
  # resolved_route: default-chat -> policy: rp-889 (geo-split), selected_pool: eu-west-1-burst? fallback_pool: us-east-1-reserved
  # policy_ttl_seconds: 0 (overrides present)

- Live trace (proxy-level):
  grpcurl -plaintext -H "x-request-id: 20260309-17:26:03-abc123" api.gateway.local sm.rt.Engine/Trace
  # trace showed: route-decide -> cache-lookup (miss) -> policy-eval -> remote forward to us-east-1-reserved -> backend returns 502 with body "incompatible-weights-quant" -> proxy returns 502

- KV cache inspection (prefix caching):
  redis-cli -h kvcache-eu-west-1 GET "prefix:20260309:20260309-17:26"
  # empty
  redis-cli -h kvcache-us-east-1 KEYS "prefix:20260309:*" | wc -l
  # large number -> suggests warm-up happened in us-east and not eu-west

Important error snippets captured from logs (these are cut/paste style; anonymized):
- 2026-03-09T17:26:06Z ERROR backend-handler: model-init failed: loader error: quant-file-mismatch (expected dim 512, got 256) -> returning 502
- 2026-03-09T17:26:07Z WARN router: fallback chosen: pool=us-east-1-reserved latency_est=320ms policy_eval=geo-split rp-889
- 2026-03-09T17:26:07Z ERROR proxy: tls-handshake-timeout to us-east-1-reserved after 10s
- 2026-03-09T17:26:10Z CRIT autoscaler: unexpected node termination during drain window - node id i-0a12... - reason=maintenance-tag

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Race between maintenance drain in eu-west-1 (nodes drained) and geo-split policy TTL/decision leading to fallback to us-east-1. The fallback path resolved to a pool with incompatible model variant (different quantization profile) causing 502s.
   - Evidence: maintenance at 17:18Z; first 5xx at 17:25Z. Logs show "incompatible-weights-quant".
2) Policy TTL bug: some route policies were evaluated with TTL=0 (force evaluation) but resolution cache was stale and returned remote pool instead of local fallback.
   - Evidence: rtrctl showed policy_ttl_seconds: 0 for rp-889 during test resolve. Also redis cache misses in eu-west.
3) Egress NAT or egress-security group misconfig in eu-west caused proxy to prefer remote pools because local forward failed quickly.
   - Evidence: tls-handshake-timeout towards us-east was observed but that might be proxy->backend. Need more networking telemetry.
4) Binarization / model variant mislabeling during autoscaler re-provisioning: new nodes in eu-west drawn from image set v2.1 while us-east used v2.0 causing mismatch for quant files. (less likely but possible)

Immediate follow-ups I did / results:
- Forced policy evaluation reset: rtrctl policy-reset rp-889 --region eu-west-1 (17:59Z) -> subsequent test resolves to local dedicated pool.
- Pinned route in emergency: rtrctl pin-route default-chat --pool dedicated-gpu-eu-west-1 (18:05Z)
- Replayed failing request with patched headers to see deterministic behavior: curl -v ... -H "x-debug-forced-pool: dedicated-gpu-eu-west-1" -> succeeded.

What I did NOT see / missing signals:
- No clear EV for node image mismatch: need infra image manifest logs.
- Traces between 17:18-17:25 from the host proxy are partially truncated on the collector (collector-ops said buffer overflow). Ask observability to re-ingest raw traces if possible.
- Network path RTT matrix for that 7-minute window is limited; need VPC flow logs.

Notes for postmortem / questions to investigate:
- Why did policy TTL become 0 for rp-889? PRs in infra show a recent change to allow dynamic TTL updates (github:infra/route-policy#198). Could be shipped without integration test.
- Confirm model registry tagging: Are pools allowed to serve multiple quant profiles under the same model name? If so, we need stronger compatibility checks at routing time.
- Autoscaler interaction: are we allowed to drain entire availability-zone-local pools while still serving traffic from local pool? We have a safeguard but it seems it kicked in too late.
- Collector truncation: fix buffer sizing for proxy trace collector during incident surges.

Todo / checklist (owned by me unless assigned):
- [ ] Pull infra image manifests for eu-west nodes during 17:00-18:30Z (assign infra: Marcus)
- [ ] Export VPC flow logs for eu-west-1 for the 17:10-18:30Z window (assign netops: Eleni)
- [ ] Add integration test for route-policy TTL 0 semantics (assign eng-serving-runtime)
- [ ] Implement pre-forward model-compatibility check: route selection should validate model signature (quant dims, tokenizers) before selecting pool (eng-ml)
- [ ] Follow up on collector overflow incident and increase buffer/enqueue or backpressure (observability)

Quick snippets to reproduce locally (for devs):
- Simulated resolve that showed remote fallback:
  # emulate policy resolver
  python -c "import json; print(json.dumps({'policy':'rp-889','chosen':'us-east-1-reserved','reason':'local-pool-drained'}))"

- To test model compatibility check (dev harness):
  ./model-compat-check --model-name redwood-open-13b --pool us-east-1-reserved
  # expected output (when incompatible): exit code 2, stderr: "quant-dim-mismatch"

Brain dump / random notes:
- Could add a routing preflight that is run under heavy-drain conditions: check local pool health + model-compat before falling back.
- Consider a short cooldown after maintenance-tagged drains before policy TTLs can fall through to global fallback.
- Slack refs: #ops-incident (thread ts 1678305600.000200), pinged @Eleni at 17:28.

Unresolved / open questions for PM/Eng:
- SLO impact: exact # of affected customers (need billing logs). Customer success already flagged 3 customers; get list.
- Should we add an explicit "compatible-pools" mapping in the model catalog to avoid cross-pool variant collisions?

Small post-incident notes to myself:
- Keep the sample request-ids — they help reconstruct trace trees. Save them in a separate artifact store rather than copy-pasting in docs.
- Don't trust console per-route health during active autoscaler events — it masked local node drains for ~7 minutes.
- Follow up with the maintainers of github:infra/route-policy#198; it looks like TTL semantics were changed without a rollout gate.

End of scratchpad. Will formalize into a postmortem doc once infra logs & VPC flows are in (blocking items above).
